voiceover: Two thousand to two thousand nine. <break time="500ms"/> Right away, eggs break from the pack. An avian flu scare in two thousand three pushes them up. By two thousand four, they're already about thirty percent above the baseline — more of your paycheck for the same dozen. Then a global commodity surge in two thousand seven and eight drives them higher. By two thousand eight, eggs are the clear outlier — nearly seventy-five percent more of your weekly wage than they cost in two thousand.

visual.description: Race chart animates 2000→2009. Chapter marker 'ACT 1: THE DIVERGENCE' fades in top-left in Montserrat Bold 36px, then fades to 20% opacity. All 6 lines begin moving from the starting position. Eggs (Muted Pink, thick line) immediately breaks upward — reaching ~1.31 by 2004, then surging to ~1.73 by 2008. At year 2001, a brief 'how to read' overlay appears for 3 seconds: arrow up = 'More expensive relative to wages', arrow down = 'Cheaper', horizontal = 'Same as 2000'. Egg RUPI value tooltip tracks the line: '1.31' at 2004, '1.73' at 2008. Other lines visible but not highlighted.
